cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Asset-light service model with no manufacturing and no backward or forward integration disclosed. The DRHP states affirmatively that 'Our Company is not in the business of manufacturing and therefore, the Company has not undertaken any steps for capacity/facility creation' (PDF p.255), and that 'We do not own any immovable property' - the Registered Office, Corporate Office and all 136 India centres operate from leased or rented premises, or from premises provided by Licensed Professionals and partner schools, on lease tenures of 11 months to 3 years (Our Business - Properties, PDF p.241). Upstream inputs are limited to centre fit-outs (interior, electrical, furniture, branding), initial inventory of therapy material and technology hardware (printers, laptops), all procured against quotations from third-party contractors and vendors and certified by an Independent Architect (Objects of the Issue, PDF p.117-118); immovable fit-out capex is approximately 30-37% of total centre capex for Company Learning Centres and partnership centres and under 9% for School Collaboration Centres, and is not recoverable if a lease ends (Risk Factor 1). Forward reach is through owned centre formats plus revenue-share partnerships with Licensed Professionals (who provide premises and referrals) and with schools, complemented by e-therapy delivered digitally and home-delivered learning kits built on an in-house library of 2,000+ teaching tools developed by a seven-person R&D team. The Company also runs an in-house Upskilling Academy for clinician training and a Centre for Excellence and Research. ABSENCES, ATTRIBUTED: the DRHP discloses NO order book, order-in-hand or unexecuted-contract value anywhere (searched the full document for 'order book', 'orders in hand', 'unexecuted' - zero hits); NO top-1/top-5/top-10 customer concentration table and NO supplier or vendor concentration table are printed in any section (Business, Risk Factors, Other Financial Information or MD&A); and NO B2B versus B2C revenue split percentage is printed - the only B2B/B2C distinction in the document is in the expected-credit-loss note, where trade receivables as at March 31, 2026 are split as B2C Rs 1.58 million and corporate/B2B Rs 113.16 million (standalone) plus Mom's Belief US Inc. Rs 68.66 million, which is a receivables ageing, not a revenue mix. NOTE ON BASIS: the domestic_export_mix percentages above are on a '% of total income' basis (MD&A Results of Operations table, PDF p.368) - the only basis on which the DRHP prints a consolidated domestic percentage. On a '% of Revenue from Operations' basis the DRHP prints export of services at 25.56% (FY26), 39.64% (FY25) and 34.12% (FY24) but prints no domestic total, only its three sub-lines. Overseas-centre (USA) revenue is a third bucket outside both domestic and export, at 41.53% of total income in FY26.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- A quarter of revenue rests on agreements with entities the Promoter controls, so it is neither arm's-length demand nor independently renewable; the DRHP also flags 50.21% of Fiscal 2025 Pro Forma Revenue from Operations on the same basis, and the receivables against these services are what turned operating cash flow negative
- All 136 India centres, the Registered Office, the Corporate Office and the US centres are leased (91 of 136 India centres are in premises not owned by the Company); a landlord refusing renewal strands the fit-out spend, and the entire Rs 413.61 million New Centre capex plan is fit-out on someone else's property
- These practitioners are independent, supply the physical space and control the referral funnel; termination or a lapse in coordination removes both the client pipeline and the location at once
- The Company plans to more than treble its network in three years while every added centre carries costs before revenue; the Company already reports time and cost overruns in setting up centres, has had negative operating cash flow in Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2026, and the funding plan is not appraised by any bank or independent agency
- Over 340 full-time clinical professionals as of March 31, 2026 with average monthly attrition of 4.41% for clinical staff; the specialist NDD pool is thin, thinnest in the Tier 3 cities the expansion targets, and inability to staff a centre forces service curtailment or costly relocation
- Mom's Belief US, Inc. and Allergy & Immunology Virginia, LLC were acquired only on June 23, 2025 and operate an allergy/asthma/immunology practice rather than the core NDD business; the Pro Forma Consolidated Financial Information for Fiscal 2025 is illustrative only and Fiscal 2026 consolidated numbers are not comparable to the prior standalone years
- Diagnosis and enrolment depend on families overcoming stigma and misconceptions, particularly in semi-urban and rural India; low enrolment, mid-programme discontinuation and payment constraints directly hit centre utilisation and revenue
- The DRHP states there are no listed Indian peers in a directly comparable business, so investors cannot benchmark the Issue Price; separately, none of the directors hold formal clinical qualifications or specialised expertise in the Company's field, leaving clinical oversight to Clinical/Medical Directors below Board level

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Set up 319 new centres across India between Fiscal 2027 and Fiscal 2029, funded with Rs 413.61 million of Issue proceeds, phased 92 centres in Fiscal 2027, 159 in Fiscal 2028 and 68 in Fiscal 2029.**
- **Set up 190 Company Learning Centres and Company Learning Centres in partnership with Licensed Professionals (average carpet area 1,500 sq. ft.) at a cost of Rs 268.84 million, phased 48 / 95 / 47 across Fiscals 2027-2029.**
- **Set up 121 School Collaboration Centres (average carpet area 300 sq. ft.) at a cost of Rs 55.35 million, phased 42 / 61 / 18 across Fiscals 2027-2029, from a base of 11 such centres as of March 31, 2026.**
- **Set up 3 Centres of Excellence and Research (average carpet area 5,000 sq. ft., one per year) at a cost of Rs 24.54 million, to validate new approaches and integrate AI/ML and predictive modelling into therapy services; note the Our …**
- **Set up 5 in-house Upskilling Academies (average carpet area 3,025 sq. ft.) at a cost of Rs 20.45 million, phased 1 / 2 / 2 across Fiscals 2027-2029; note the Our Business chapter instead describes seven new Upskilling Academies, and the …**
- **Deploy Rs 144.45 million of Net Proceeds on lease payments for existing India centres, phased Rs 45.82 million in Fiscal 2027, Rs 48.11 million in Fiscal 2028 and Rs 50.52 million in Fiscal 2029.**
- **Invest Rs 101.31 million of Net Proceeds in wholly owned Subsidiary Mom's Belief US Inc. for lease/licence payments on the existing US centres, phased Rs 32.83 million / Rs 33.73 million / Rs 34.74 million across Fiscals 2027-2029.**
- **Spend Rs 102.08 million of Net Proceeds on brand awareness and inclusive outreach programs, phased Rs 18.02 million in Fiscal 2027, Rs 34.04 million in Fiscal 2028 and Rs 50.02 million in Fiscal 2029.**
- **Extend the centre network to more than 25 states and union territories in India, from 20 states and union territories and 57 cities as of March 31, 2026, balanced across Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.**
- **Establish behaviour therapy support services at the three acquired centres in Virginia, USA over the next three years, extending them beyond their current allergy, asthma and immunology practice.**
- **Expand operations into the United Arab Emirates and the United Kingdom through group entities Carving Futures SPV Limited (UAE) and Carving Futures UK Private Limited (UK), which have been incorporated for that purpose.**
- **Newly opened centres are expected to require approximately 8 to 12 months to reach operational breakeven - the yardstick against which the 319-centre rollout should be graded.**
